summary_note: Amarillo Endoscopy paper tracking systems were determined to be legitimate operational tools; however, an employee at Lubbock OPC reported desired-date substitution practices linked to prior supervisory instruction, creating evidence of improper scheduling behavior without broader corroboration of systemic manipulation.
Fabricated veteran contact-date concerns suggested problematic documentation practices but not fully substantiated fraud.
Retroactive appointment creation reflected documentation of same-day outreach encounters rather than concealment.

Consult delays stemmed from provider shortages; consult closures and EWL usage followed policy.
Radiology no-show cancellation practices followed legacy guidance and were not found to constitute manipulation.
Tracking spreadsheets were known to management and used operationally for continuity of care; OIG did not substantiate concealment or intentional wait-time manipulation.

Fort Worth OPC staff confirmed scheduling practices inconsistent with VHA Directive requirements, including desired-date handling problems; however, evidence suggested systemic training and VistA workflow confusion, and management had begun corrective actions prior to investigation.

Weekly over-14-day scheduling reports were circulated and multiple MSAs confirmed routine zeroing-out practices; at least one employee reported explicit instruction to manipulate desired dates while another described an implied coercive environment with feared repercussions for noncompliance.
OIG did not substantiate destruction of wait-list information; operational transition issues predominated.

OIG identified desired-date substitution practices in which negotiated or next-available appointment dates were entered instead of veterans? true requested dates, producing artificially reduced wait times.
Pressure existed to use next available dates and optimize scheduling metrics, though evidence of organized fraud was limited.

Although initial findings emphasized operational scheduling deficiencies, subsequent evidence tied to Tallahassee OPC identified directed manipulation, post-Phoenix concealment behavior, and witness intimidation under the Gainesville administrative structure.
Spreadsheet tracking was validated as an operational VISN-supported process tool.

OIG identified systematic ?backing out? scheduling methods, suppression of EWL use, and fabricated access metrics sustained through improper staff training until corrective scheduling enforcement began in January 2014; findings were referred to VA Accountability Review.
Excel tracking systems created the appearance of 14-day compliance while veterans waited substantially longer.
Scheduling errors and shortages existed, but intentional manipulation was not substantiated.
Schedulers were trained to use appointment dates as desired dates to create zero-day waits.
High-profile allegations regarding suicides and delayed psychiatric care could not be substantiated.

Investigation identified negligence by an individual scheduling clerk who failed to process approximately 1,032 follow-up ?yellow sheet? requests; management self-reported the issue and immediately scheduled delayed appointments, with no evidence of institutional wait-time gaming or metric manipulation.
Paper logbook functioned as an operational duplicate scheduler rather than a concealed wait list.
Paper scheduling allegations lacked corroborating evidence and specific examples.
Allegations regarding miscoded cancellations for financial benefit were not substantiated.

Supervisors and schedulers systematically manipulated desired dates, deleted comments, overbooked appointments, and zeroed out waits.

Investigations involving Louisville and Dupont CBOC did not substantiate systemic wait-time manipulation; concerns were largely tied to workplace disputes and differing interpretations of scheduling procedures, while Dupont scheduling practices were found compliant with Directive 2010-027.
OIG documented desired-date manipulation, EWL avoidance, consult discontinuance, leadership pressure, and performance-driven wait-time gaming.
Paper tracking lists were operational workarounds rather than intentional wait-time manipulation.
Scheduling confusion existed, but secret lists and deliberate concealment were not substantiated.

Two reports; no manipulation substantiated; Access database legitimate clinical tool

Across Tennessee Valley Healthcare System facilities, OIG identified management-directed desired-date replacement practices, systematic zeroing-out of wait times, and a coercive scheduling culture involving feared repercussions for noncompliance. Although one investigation did not substantiate records concealment allegations, the combined evidence across Chattanooga and Murfreesboro supported systemic wait-time manipulation behaviors.
Schedulers were trained to use next available dates as desired dates, creating distorted metrics through improper training.
Desired-date misuse stemmed from inadequate understanding of scheduling procedures rather than management pressure or deliberate metric manipulation; OIG identified no gaming schemes or patient harm.

At the Chehalis CBOC, fewer than 10 desired-date changes were identified over a three-year period and were characterized as clerical corrections; OIG found no documentary evidence of direction to manipulate wait-time metrics.
Multiple investigations substantiated desired-date manipulation, cancellation/rescheduling practices, and explicit zero-out scheduling behavior.
Supervisors encouraged schedulers to offer next available appointments first, creating pressure toward metric-oriented scheduling behavior.
Mental Health scheduling staff faced sustained pressure to alter desired dates and maintain zero-day waits, with adverse patient-care implications.

Managers directed staff to zero out wait times in violation of scheduling policy.

Facility fact-finding confirmed use of paper tracking lists outside official scheduling systems; multiple witnesses contradicted denials by scheduling staff, and supervisory personnel demonstrated inadequate understanding of Directive 2010-027, supporting systemic improper scheduling practices.
OIG substantiated use of incorrect desired dates and appointment gaming tied to performance metrics and leadership incentives.
